en: The Philippines is an archipelago composed of exactly 7,641 islands.
Mount Apo is the highest mountain in the Philippines, standing at 2,954 meters above sea level.
Mount Taal is the second most active volcano in the Philippines, with 38 historical eruptions.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering an area of about 911 square kilometers.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park covers 96,828 hectares of pristine marine habitat in the Sulu Sea.
Palawan is the largest province in the Philippines by land area, covering 14,649 square kilometers.
The Sierra Madre mountain range stretches 540 kilometers, making it the longest mountain range in the Philippines.
The Philippines experiences an average of 20 tropical cyclones every year, entering the Philippine Area of Responsibility.
Maria Cristina Falls in Lanao del Norte drops 98 meters, making it one of the highest waterfalls in the Philippines.
The Philippines had about 7.1 million hectares of forest cover in 2020, representing roughly 23 percent of its total land area.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an 8.2-kilometer long underground river flowing directly into the sea.
